Restaurant's favorite review
Pho with hot stone 🍲
Feb 2025 • Solo
Affordable price, i came and ask the staff if they accept card for payment but the staff cant speak english, so i need to wait until 1 staff come and talk to me, i think only one staff who can speak english. Order the one with hot stone, so we need to put by ourselves the noodles, meat and other vegetable into the hot stone fill with the soup. Because i not put all of them in one time, the soup not boil enough and my meat not cooked well, lol, so i ask the staff who can speak english to boil again my soup, and voila..they also adding my soup.

The taste really yummy, the meat so tender, the noodles also fresh and they give so many vegetables, the soup is super tasty, love it. The restaurant really crowd, but more guest come with family. The condiment available in the table and the drink (looks like tea) also avail in the table, free charge, free refill. I got trouble with my payment, but thanks for the cashier want to wait until the issued solved. The restroom also clean and provide westafel.

Best Pho in HCMC
Jan 2026 • Solo
If you only have time for one bowl of Pho in Saigon, make it Pho Museum. I can honestly say this is the best Pho in the city—the broth is incredibly flavorful and clear, and the ingredients are exceptionally fresh.

The restaurant itself is spotless, inviting, and beautifully decorated, creating a wonderful atmosphere that stands out from the crowd. What really makes the experience special, though, is the staff. They are extremely friendly and provide top-tier service that makes you feel right at home. I’m so impressed that I’ll be visiting once a day for the remainder of my trip! Highly, highly recommended.

Fo bo with a star
Jul 2025 • Solo
After a long walk, I was looking for a place to finally eat, and on the map I came across this place simply called Pho. What else do you need on your first day in Vietnam but a plate of hot Pho Bo? Especially at the entrance are painted Michelin signs - solid, it is no longer possible to pass by. The place is small: several tables and a kitchen in plain sight. It later turned out there was a second room just down the street. The menu is extensive, with pictures and English translation, so it's convenient to order. Prices are nice. The service is quick - ten minutes after the order I was already facing a big bowl of my Fo Bo. The portion is generous: lots of meat, rich broth, fresh vegetables served separately, sauces on the table. Branded dishes are small, but nice. The soup turned out to be delicious and satisfying. Exactly what it takes to officially consider a day in Vietnam a success.
